kd_walker.text: The Pilgrims' Way runs from Winchester all the way to Canterbury. They reckon Chaucer's lot came down from London on Watling Street instead, the A2 now.
Either way, pilgrims bought souvenir badges at the shrine and wore them home on their hats. People find them in the Thames mud even now.

kd_hop_farmer.text: Hops are for beer: they make it bitter and help it keep. Before hops, English ale was sweet and went off in days.
Every bine goes up its string clockwise. Try to make one go the other way and it'll unwind itself overnight. Stubborn things. Like farmers.

kd_cobnut_seller.text: Kentish cobnuts! A kind of hazelnut, grown in plats in the Weald. Eat them fresh in August while they're green and milky, or wait till they're brown and crack them by the fire.
My great-gran picked them for the London markets. She could fill a basket faster than a squirrel, and the squirrels hated her for it.

then.text: My tale's told. Go and hear the others, and tell the Host I was the best.
A verray, parfit, gentil knyght. Very perfect, gentle, and not at all wanting to fight you, unless the Host says so. He says so.
My tale is of two cousins, Palamon and Arcite, prisoners in Athens, who both fall for the lady Emelye from their tower window.
They fight for her in a great tournament. Arcite wins, then his horse throws him and he dies. Palamon marries Emelye in the end. Knights' tales are long. That is the short version.

else.text: I'm saving my tale for the road. The Host at the Chequer of Hope in Canterbury is judging a contest, if you'd care to hear it.

then.text: My tale's told. Go and hear the others, and tell the Host I was the best.
I'm the Miller. Chaucer says I could break a door off its hinges by running at it with my head. I've had a drink. Let's go.
My tale's about a carpenter, his young wife, and a lodger who tricks the carpenter into sleeping in a tub in the roof to escape a second Noah's flood.
It ends with a misplaced kiss, a red-hot poker, and the carpenter crashing through the ceiling. Chaucer apologised for it in advance. I don't.
